key_insight: Magnetically driven swirl in liquid metal electrodes follows a Ruelle–Takens–Newhouse route to chaos, with an intermediate strange non-chaotic attractor regime.
engineering_relevance: The Lorentz-to-viscous force ratio Q_m helps organize flow transitions at fixed aspect ratio, informing electromagnetic flow control in liquid metal batteries.
method: Three-dimensional simulations of cylindrical liquid metal electrodes under applied currents of 11.11–100 A.
Varied vertical magnetic field from 0.1–20 G, cylinder radius from 3–9 cm, and height between 3 and 4.5 cm.
Diagnosed transitions using phase portraits, FFT spectra, the 0–1 chaos test, autocorrelation, and correlation dimension.
evidence_signal: Across simulated geometries and forcing conditions, the oscillation-onset Q_m was nearly invariant at fixed aspect ratio except when height changed, while Reynolds number followed Re ∼ Q_m^(2/3).
watch_item: Height-dependent onset thresholds limit a universal Q_m criterion, and experimental validation is not reported in the abstract.
paper_title: Transition to turbulence in swirl created by a vertical magnetic field in liquid metal electrodes
